identity: A resizable panel, text box, table column, or pair of panes has a handle, border, or divider that changes its size.

scenarios.name: numeric
scenarios.screen: One window-like panel starts at a size different from its stated target. A resize handle sits on its edge or corner, and the panel shows either a live size readout or pixel marks along its fixed edges.
never: A panel already at its target size

arrangements.text: The panel sits on the left with a corner handle at its lower right and a size readout inside it.
The panel sits on the right with an edge handle on its left side and pixel marks along its fixed edges.

scenarios.hint: Give the panel enough expansion room; no numeric input shortcut.

scenarios.name: ghost
scenarios.screen: One window-like panel starts at a different size from a dashed target outline. The outline and panel share a fixed corner, and a resize handle sits on the panel's edge or corner.
never: A panel that already matches the outline

arrangements.text: The panel and outline share their upper-left corner, with the panel's handle at its lower right.
The panel and outline share their upper-right corner, with the panel's handle at its lower left.

scenarios.hint: Show the named resizable panel with a corner handle and a larger dashed target outline. Start panel and ghost differ in width and height. Target outline fully fits the work area.

scenarios.name: relative
scenarios.screen: One window-like panel starts at a size different from the relative goal. It has a resize handle and either a live size readout or pixel marks; a named reference element is also visible when the goal compares the panel with another element.
never: A reference element that can be resized

arrangements.text: The resizable panel sits to the left of the named reference element, with its handle at the lower-right corner.
The named reference element sits above the resizable panel, whose handle is on its right edge.

scenarios.name: textarea
scenarios.screen: A filled text box starts at a size different from its goal and has the browser's resize grip at its lower-right corner. An exact-size goal shows a size caption below the box, while an outline goal shows a dashed target outline.
never: A custom handle on another corner
A text box already at its exact target size

arrangements.text: The text box sits above its size caption, with the native grip at the box's lower-right corner.
The text box starts from the outline's upper-left corner, with the outline extending beyond the box.

scenarios.name: column
scenarios.screen: A filled data table has several named columns and rows. The target header has a draggable right border; a column-width bar appears below the table in most starts, with a ruler there in the others.
never: A draggable border between body cells only

arrangements.text: The table sits above the column-width bar, with the target header between other columns.
The table sits above a ruler, with the target header at the left edge of the table.

scenarios.name: split
scenarios.screen: Two named panes start at a division different from the goal, with a draggable divider between them. Size readouts appear when this start includes them.
never: A floating resize handle away from the divider
Panes already divided at the target position

arrangements.text: The first pane sits left of the second pane, with a vertical divider between them.
The first pane sits above the second pane, with a horizontal divider between them.

scenarios.name: aspect
scenarios.screen: One window-like panel starts at a size different from its goal. It has a resize handle and an aspect-lock toggle inside the panel; the goal keeps the panel's starting proportions.
never: A panel already at its goal size

arrangements.text: The panel has a lower-right corner handle, with the aspect-lock toggle inside it.
The panel has a handle on its right edge, with the aspect-lock toggle inside it.
